preamble: Depalatalization (hardening) of [bʲ] to plain [b] removes the palatal secondary articulation. In Slavic it is especially visible with labials: Proto-Slavic word-final soft labials stayed soft in Russian (голубь [ˈɡoɫʊpʲ], gen. голубя) but hardened in Ukrainian and in Czech and Slovak, where the inflected forms show plain [b] throughout the paradigm.

examples.note: Ukrainian has no final devoicing, so the hardened [b] surfaces directly; contrast Russian голубь [ˈɡoɫʊpʲ], gen. голубя, which keeps the soft labial.
Czech lost the palatalized labials altogether; the genitive holuba shows plain /b/ (the nominative is devoiced word-finally). Slovak holub, gen. holuba, is parallel.

sources: Shevelov, G. Y. (1979). A Historical Phonology of the Ukrainian Language. Carl Winter Universitätsverlag.
